chapter: Later tours, illness and the union job
title: Time away from the horn and a swollen lip
summary: He tried playing with Jimmy Rushing at the Half Note, but his lip swelled, so he stayed home, and reflects on forty years of playing.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Now I don't know how long it's going to take exactly before I, you know, start practicing again. Because I know it wasn't right when I went down to, I played with Jimmy Rushing at the Half Note. last March, but it wasn't right. And I only played one night out of three. I was supposed to play Friday, Saturday and Sunday. So I played one night. The next day my lip had all swollen up. I think that comes from inactivity.
Yes, I mean I suppose that would be normal.

Yes. My lips swelled up. So I just said, I think I just started too early. So I'm not going to do that again. So for a long time I just did nothing. Except stay at home. Cut the grass, rake the leaves, look at television, and drank beer.
And that was really a unique experience for you.
No,no. But it gets tiresome, you know.
Oh sure. Well I mean after you've lived a very active life.

Well yes, you see, I can't really complain too much because from the age of twenty to sixty it's been a constant playing somewhere. In different countries and making money. I don't expect to play for ever.
